description: Keeps each task definition's pinned image digest current within the tag it names, and each image under images/ current with its base and the tool versions it pins.
Renovate merges its own pull requests rather than using GitHub's auto-merge, which waits only for required checks; main requires none, so it would merge before lint finished.
Schedules are in UTC, Renovate's default: each day's updates are batched before 06:00 UTC.

customManagers.description: The image a task definition pins: the tag in the comment directly above exec.image, and the digest on that line.
A tool version an image's Dockerfile pins in an ARG, named by the `# renovate:` comment directly above it.

blender.description: Blender publishes no release feed, only a download directory per release line.

packageRules.description: A definition is pinned to one release line, so its vendor image never moves to another major version. A new line is a new definition, added by hand. A swale-built image's major version is its tool's, moved by an image change already reviewed.
Python's release line is its minor version, so a Python definition takes patch releases only. Renovate offers the newest minor and patch as one update unless told to keep them apart.
Python's release line is its minor version, so a Python definition takes patch releases only.
One pull request a day for every definition whose vendor image has a new build or release within its line. It merges itself once lint passes.
Releases that can change behavior within a version line wait for review, each in its own pull request: vLLM is still 0.x, and every llama.cpp build is a release.
A swale-built image is tagged with its tool's version, plus -r<N> for each rebuild on that version. Renovate's Docker versioning would read -r1 as a different variant and never offer it.
swaleio/ollama still carries 1.0.0, its tag from before images were tagged by their tool's version, which outranks Ollama's own 0.x versions. Drop this once that tag is deleted from Docker Hub.

A swale-built image is published from a change that already built here, so definitions follow it as soon as it lands, in one pull request that merges itself once lint passes. A major version waits for review.
Merging an image change publishes the image. A rebuilt base or a patch release merges itself once the image builds; a minor or major release waits for review.
One pull request for every image whose base was rebuilt upstream that day.
A distribution base moves to a new release by hand; only its digest is kept current.
alpine/git tags each release twice, as 2.54.1 and v2.54.1; stay on the form without the v.
Blender's download directory lists every file of every release in the line; the version is read from the Linux build's file name.
Each PowerShell image stays on its own release line.

The Hugging Face training stack is pinned in two images, which move together.
The linter's npm dependencies. A patch or minor update merges itself once its checks pass; a major update changes how the linter reads YAML, so it waits for review.
